handbookNote: North Dakota 2025-2027 Commercial Driver License Manual, Class A, B and C (base AAMVA '2005 Model Commercial Driver License Manual', Rev. July 2014, with North Dakota-specific front matter and a North Dakota-specific 'Modernized Commercial Driver License Skills Test' supplement), published by the North Dakota Department of Transportation (NDDOT) Driver License Division -- confirmed as the current, unchanged administering agency via dot.nd.gov/driver/commercial/commercial-driver-license and dot.nd.gov/driver/commercial/commercial-driver-license-manual on 2026-08-23 (no agency transition has occurred here, unlike Oklahoma's DPS-to-Service Oklahoma or South Dakota's DPS-to-ServiceNow-portal transitions seen elsewhere in this project) -- fetched directly from https://www.dot.nd.gov/sites/www/files/documents/Drivers%20-%20documents/commercial%20vehicles/CDL-manual.pdf on 2026-08-23 (10.7MB PDF, linked from NDDOT's own 'Commercial Driver License Manual' page, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/nd_cdl_research/nd_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,814 lines, cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction, nd_cdl_manual_raw.txt, 13,466 lines, for any column-misaligned tables or OCR-garbled passages, particularly in the Hazardous Materials hazard-class table and the Vehicle/Basic-Control Skills Test sections). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are HEDGED: North Dakota's own manual never discloses a specific number of items per knowledge test or an explicit passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for 'questions', '80%', 'percent', 'passing score', and similar terms across both extractions, which surfaced only generic references such as 'these questions may be on your test' and procedural material (e.g. knowledge-test appointment rules, a same-day retest ban after any failed test, $5 per-attempt cost, audio testing availability at all eight driver license offices) with no item count or score threshold ever stated. The federally standardized minimum passing score of 80% under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless, and North Dakota's own manual explicitly requires each skills-test component (vehicle inspection, basic control, on-road) to be passed independently before advancing to the next. A major North Dakota-specific structural feature, preserved rather than smoothed over: effective December 1, 2025, North Dakota began a hybrid rollout (continuing throughout 2026) of a new 'Modernized Commercial Driver License Skills Test' that changes the Airbrake/Hydraulic Brake Check, Vehicle Inspection, and Basic Control Skills portions of the skills test -- the manual therefore contains BOTH the legacy test content (Section 11 Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test) AND the new modernized content (Section 11M Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 12M Basic Control Skills Test) side by side, with real, distinct, ND-sourced procedural differences between them (e.g. the legacy air brake check's low-air warning activates below 60 psi with the tractor protection valve popping out at approximately 40 psi, while the modernized 11M check's low-air warning activates below 55 psi with the valve popping out between 20-45 psi; the modernized test also uses a qualitative/explain-and-demonstrate approach versus the legacy test's more prescriptive walk-through). Which version an applicant takes depends on the driver license site and is confirmed by NDDOT via phone/email per the manual's own front-matter notice. North Dakota's driver license classes are A (combination vehicles, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,001 lbs GVWR/GVW), B (single vehicle 26,001+ lbs GVWR, may tow a vehicle not over 10,000 lbs), C (single vehicle 26,000 lbs or less designed to transport 16+ passengers including the driver, or placarded for hazardous materials, may tow a vehicle not over 10,000 lbs), D (noncommercial, with its own farm-vehicle, custom-harvester, and covered-farm-vehicle exemptions under NDCC 39-06.2-06/-09 and 49 CFR 390.5), and M (two- or three-wheeled motorcycle, requiring a separate endorsement on top of a Class A/B/C/D license). Endorsements are H (Hazardous Materials, requiring a TSA Security Threat Assessment/fingerprint background check per 49 CFR 383.71 and USA PATRIOT Act screening), N (Tank Vehicle, individual tank rated capacity over 119 gallons AND aggregate rated capacity of 1,000+ gallons), P (Passenger, 16+ passengers including driver), T (Doubles/Triples), and S (School Bus, 16+ passengers including driver, transporting students); the H and T endorsements are not allowed on Commercial Learner's Permits, while P and S are allowed on CLPs with no passengers other than a supervising driver/examiner, and N is allowed on CLPs restricted to empty tanks only. North Dakota's own CDL-specific restriction-code set is E (no manual transmission), K (intrastate only), L (no airbrake-equipped CMV), M (no Class A passenger bus), N (no Class A or B passenger bus), O (no tractor-trailer CMV), P (no passengers on a Learner's Permit with P/S endorsement), V (medical variance), X (empty tanks only on a Learner's Permit with N endorsement), and Z (no full-airbrake-equipped CMV) -- a distinct 10-code set from other states in this project. North Dakota uses a 4-category federal medical-certification framework (Category 1 Interstate/49 CFR 391, Category 2 Interstate-but-excepted, Category 3 Intrastate/state-qualification, Category 4 Intrastate-and-excepted) tied to the FMCSA National Registry's electronic medical-examiner-certificate transmission (effective June 23, 2025), and mandates federal Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) before a first-time Class A/B license, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time School Bus/Passenger/Hazardous Materials endorsement. Content-depth rationale: North Dakota uses the identical AAMVA-authored '2005 Model Commercial Driver License Manual' (Rev. July 2014) base document already used by several other CDL-track states in this project (e.g. New Mexico, Louisiana), organized into the same 13 core sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.24 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Airbrakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.8 the Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, and -- reflecting North Dakota's unique dual legacy/modernized skills-test structure -- Section 11 Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection Test plus Section 11M Vehicle Inspection Test combined into one bucket (13_vehicle_inspection), and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test plus Section 12M Basic Control Skills Test plus Section 13 On-Road Driving combined into one bucket (14_basic_control_onroad), with North Dakota-specific administrative detail (license classes, endorsements, restriction codes, ELDT, medical certification categories, farm/covered-farm-vehicle exemptions, testing procedures, and the Modernized Skills Test transition notice) layered into the licensing bucket (01_licensing) from the manual's own North Dakota-specific front matter. Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Air Brakes, Hazardous Materials, School Buses, and the dual-format Vehicle Inspection section supported deeper coverage than initially targeted and were sized up accordingly. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official North Dakota manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds for both the legacy and modernized tests, tank endorsement capacity thresholds, hazmat parking/attendance distances, weight/capacity figures, endorsement and restriction-code definitions) were verified against the actual North Dakota text read by the drafting process, not assumed from other states' manuals even where those states share the same AAMVA base document. Final pool: 725 questions across 14 buckets, independently re-verified by the top-level build process (not just drafting sub-agent self-reports) for JSON validity, required-field completeness, four-distinct-choices-per-question, and A/B/C/D answer-letter balance (final tally 181/184/181/179, each 24.7-25.4% of the pool).
